author: nero_eth
content:
I agree and think this situation is not straightforward to resolve.
I wanted to write-up a post about worst-case blocks anyway and included a section on FOCIL:
https://ethresear.ch/t/whats-a-block-and-how-big-can-it-get/26281

The tldr is, there are two size limits, 10 mib on the CL msg, 8 mib on the EL block.
There are situations where a block is below 8 mib on the EL but above 10 mib on the CL. The EL, while building the block, cannot reason about the 10 mib cap of the CL, and what might look fine on the EL, could already exceed accepted limits on the CL.
What focil needs is a max-gas-limit (which needs to be set to ~266M) for hegota as otherwise we could exceed the 8 mib on the EL already.
Bascially, we use the max-gas-limit (newly introduced) to ensure that the size caps never actually bite.

author: chfast
content:
The RLP block size limit can be incorporated to the IL check, but is rather awkward. I would fix RLP size check instead: its goal is to guarantee CL blocks is under 10MB size, by putting 8MB limit on the RLP EL payload. So this is basically: 8MB looks smaller than 10MB. Two issues already: 1. this is not compatible with Engine API where there is no RLP block, 2. It adds new block validation rule in a new place: just after all transaction validation (this hits IL).

Better approach is the put limit on the total transaction size (same as IL already proposes): i.e. sum of size of encoded transactions. This is easy to check during transaction validation (same as gas limits). I'm guessing the other parts of the block are constant overheads or functions of the transaction sizes. <@792404665068158998> may know this already.

author: nero_eth
content:
yeah right, one issue i describe in the post is how a block can be <8mib on the EL but >10mib on the CL, and for focil inclusion checks, we'd need to reason about both if they are reachable - which they aren't if we set a max-possible-gaslimit as a hard cap for the block gas limit.
Putting a cap on the total txs won't help as other things (BAL, requests, encoding overhead, etc) could then still hit the CL limit.

author: nero_eth
content: The only clean solution I see guaranteeing that we never hit the size limits, and the only way to do so is defining and enforcing a max gas limit. Blocks pumping the gas limit higher are invalid.

author: chfast
content: But it looks the only safe limit is 300M. This will be very controversial as this is in range of promised Glamsterdam limit.

author: nero_eth
content: That's at least when the EL limits starts constraining. But yeah, for the CL it'd be at 300M, but depends on what happens with 8131+8279.
